newsitem.title: EGYPT: Palestinian refugees refuse to go back to Libya.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian refugees refuse to go back to Libya.

text.p: More than 200 Palestinian refugees who have been stranded in appalling conditions in a makeshift camp on the Libyan-Egyptian border for more than a year refused on Tuesday to go back to Libya.

The refugees, deported to the camp in 1995, argued with Libyan officials who tried to persuade them back, and staged a sit-in on the road that links the two countries, saying they would rather go to Egypt or the Palestinian self-rule areas.
The Libyan officials, accompanied by members of a Palestinian youth group, arrived at the camp in several small buses but it was not clear how they intended to transport the residents of the camp.
"We want to go to any Arab country other than Libya. We want to go to Palestine. There are 15,000 Palestinians in Libya who are unemployed," one Palestinian man told Libyan officials.

Libya threw out the Palestinians in 1995 in an attempt to discredit steps towards peace between Israel and the Palestinians. Egypt will not let them in unless they can prove a third country will give them residence.
Libya reversed the policy a week ago, saying it was not possible for the Palestinians to go home to the Palestinian-ruled territories.
Moussa Mohammed Ibrahim, the leader of the refugees, said two Libyan officials had threatened to cut off the water supply to the camp if its residents refused to go to Libya.

"The policy of your president with Israel is a failure," shouted one Libyan official at the refugees, referring to Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, whose deals with Israel give limited self-rule to Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.
The peace agreements give Israel the right to control entry into the self-rule areas.
The youth group held banners, one of which read: "Palestinians will definitely return to their homes which have been usurped by the Zionists."
The camp's residents held banners that made their desired destination clear. "Libyans, Egyptians -- our path is towards Palestine," read one.

The refugees and staff members of the international charity Medecins sans Frontieres who are permanently based in the camp asked journalists not to leave because they feared Libyan officials would use force against the Palestinians.
"Egypt, especially (President) Hosni Mubarak is the cause of this whole problem. Egypt can completely solve the camp problem," shouted one refugee.

He was referring to the tough Egyptian line on letting the refugees in. Egypt has made some exceptions in cases of emergency health problems but some of the refugees have Egyptian wives awaiting them in Egypt.

Many of the Palestinians have said they do not want to return to Libya because they do not know what awaits them there. The Libyan officials at the camp said those who were employed could go to back to their jobs.
The refugees have been living in appalling conditions in a tented encampment in no-man's-land between the Egyptian and Libyan border posts near Salloum on the Mediterranean coast.
The Palestinians had been in Libya as workers, students or with their respective families.
Sources at the border earlier said Libyan officials had taken journalists to Tobruk, bypassing the camp.
